To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stable distribution of the immune status of a population is a linear combination of the stable distributions of the immune status for individuals with different numbers of infections.

the stable distribution of antibody level in a population is given by the solution of a linear renewal equation, and that this solution is characterized by a probability distribution that is uniquely determined by the force of infection and the waning and boosting dynamics.

the distribution of immune states (as captured by the antibody level) is a linear function of the force of infection, that the stable distribution has a finite mean, and that the distribution has a finite variance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of immune system and its response to the force of infection.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the considered model, the distribution of immune statuses is a mixture of exponential distributions.
the stable distribution of the antibody level in the population is a lognormal distribution.

, for a given level of force of infection, there exists a unique stable distribution of immune statuses, and the distribution is characterized by its mean, variance, skewness and kurtosis, which are all given explicitly in terms of the force of infection and the parameters of the within-host model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stable distribution of the immune status is a mixture of gamma distributions, with the mixture coefficients depending on the force of infection and the rate of boosting.
the immune status distribution can be obtained from the force of infection, the waning function and the boost function, and vice versa.
we provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for the renewal equation approach to waning and boosting.

the distribution of immune statuses is a function of the force of infection.
